Downy_Mildew.quote: An extensive growth of sporophores on the undersurface of the mature leaves appears as white, discrete projections bearing spores.
Yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces, often angular because they are limited by the veins, with a fuzzy growth of whitish mould on the corresponding underside.

Gray_Mold.quote: Leaves on or near the soil or in the dampest areas of the garden turn light brown and develop a gray or brown fuzzy growth of fungal spores.
Lower leaves of plants infected with Botrytis yellow, and eventually the whole head wilts and rots.
Plants shrivel and rot and often develop flattened hard black masses, called sclerotia, under rotted parts.
The initial symptom is a dark, water-soaked lesion, and a soft rot of infected leaves and stems occurs as the pathogen grows into healthy tissues.

Leaf_Mosaic_Virus.quote: Leaves of plants that are infected at a young stage are stunted, deformed, and (in some varieties) show a mosaic or mottling pattern.
Such plants rarely grow to full size; head lettuce varieties that are infected early fail to form heads.

Lettuce_Chlorosis_Virus.quote: Leaves of plants infected with lettuce chlorosis virus exhibit severe yellowing, rolling, brittleness, and vein-clearing. Plants infected early are stunted.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: The flat, low-growing white to gray mycelia and spores of this fungus develop on the outside of flower bracts and on upper surfaces of both young and old leaves.

Septoria_Blight.quote: Light brown irregular spots occur between the leaf veins; these expand rapidly and cover the leaves; the leaves dry out, become papery and the centres of the spots fall out.

Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.quote: Leaves of infected plants develop brown to dark brown spots and dead (necrotic) areas.
Plants infected early in development may become stunted and then die.
